newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL-NBA'S WOMEN'S LEAGUE ASSIGNS 16 STARS TO TEAMS.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-NBA'S WOMEN'S LEAGUE ASSIGNS 16 STARS TO TEAMS.

text.p: The fledgling Women's National Basketball Association distributed its first 16 signed players, a group including U.S., Australian and Russian Olympic stars, among its eight teams on Wednesday.

After winning the gold medal last summer in Atlanta for the United States, glamorous centre Lisa Leslie was assigned to Los Angeles, currently pregnant Sheryl Swoopes went to Houston and popular Rebecca Lobo was sent to New York.

Two veteran international players were also allocated. Australia's quicksilver guard Michele Timms was assigned to Phoenix, while Utah received gritty centre-forward Elena Baranova, who played for the Unified Team in the 1992 Olympics and for Russia in 1996.
Each club in the eight-team league was allocated a guard and a frontcourt player. Players were assigned based on regional appeal and competitive considerations.
Leslie, a centre who averaged a team-best 19.5 points per game in Atlanta, is teamed in Los Angeles with Penny Toler, a two-time All-American guard from Long Beach State.

Swoopes, a forward, is joined in Houston by Cynthia Cooper, a guard from Southern California and a member of the 1988 and 1992 U.S. Olympic teams. Swoopes is expecting the birth of a boy in June, when the regular season begins, but she intends to play.

New York was given guard Teresa Weatherspoon, a two-time All-American at Louisiana Tech, in addition to Lobo, who led the University of Connecticut to an undefeated national championship that helped build interest in women's basketball ahead of the Olympics.
In addition to Timms, Phoenix received Jennifer Gillom, a centre who was on the 1988 Olympic team and played collegiately at Mississippi.
Along with Baranova, Utah got LeJuana "Lady" Hardmon, a two-time All-Southeastern Conference player from Georgia.
Sacramento was awarded guard Ruthie Bolton-Holifield, another key 1996 U.S. Olympian, and Bridgette Gordon, a 1988 Olympian who was the MVP of Tennessee's 1989 national championship team.
Charlotte was given centre Vicky Bullett, a two-time Olympian from Maryland, and guard Andrea Stinson, a two-time All-American from North Carolina State.
Cleveland received Janice Lawrence Braxton, a 1984 Olympian from Louisiana Tech, and Michelle Edwards, the 1988 Big Ten Player of the Year and All-American from Iowa.
The announcements were made by WNBA president Val Ackerman at NBA Entertainment studios.
Phoenix, Los Angeles (Lakers), Sacramento and Utah will comprise the Western Conference, while New York, Charlotte, Cleveland and Houston make up the Eastern Conference.

The two-month schedule will be released in February, as will team names and logos. The WNBA draft will take place April 28 with training camps opening May 28 and the regular season beginning June 21. Each team will play 14 home and 14 away games.

The ABL, a separate women's league not affiliated with any other basketball organisation, is already in its inaugural season with teams in Atlanta, Colorado, Columbus, New England, Portland, Richmond, San Jose and Seattle.
